acceptedAnswer.text: UI/UX design is the work of understanding how people use a website or app, then designing the flows and screens that make it easy to get done what they came to do. UX is how it works; UI is how it looks.

mainEntity.name: How does UI/UX design work with MMC?

acceptedAnswer.text: We research the users, map flows, wireframe and design screens, test clickable prototypes with real users, and package everything as a design system.
We quote per project, after a call, once the scope is clear: what you need, how much of it, and what it has to connect to. The scope and the fee are agreed in writing before work starts.
No. Nobody can guarantee a conversion lift from design alone. We commit to research, testing with real users and a clear design system, and honest reporting.

Teams building or fixing a website or app. Not only D2C. We work with D2C, B2B and education brands, and set the work up differently for each: D2C on shopping and checkout flows, B2B on enquiry and demo flows, education on course, fee and application journeys.

points.title: A system that scales

leaks.lede: Most usability problems are built in early. Each stage below is where they start, and how we design them out.

stages.breaks: Designing for what the team assumes.
stages.why: Teams know their product too well. Real users use it differently, and find different things hard.
stages.does: We interview users and study analytics, so design starts from what people actually do and where they get stuck.

stages.breaks: Arranging pages by how the business is organised.
stages.why: Users think in tasks, not in departments. A structure that follows the org chart makes tasks harder.
stages.does: We map the key journeys and rebuild the structure around the tasks people came to do.

stages.why: Visual polish on a weak flow only hides the problem. Structure comes before style.
stages.does: We move from wireframes to polished screens, checking each against the task it must support.

stages.breaks: Finding out about problems after launch.
stages.why: Fixing a problem in a prototype costs a fraction of fixing it in a live product.
stages.does: We build clickable prototypes and test them with real users before development starts.

stages.why: Without shared components, sites drift and every change takes longer.
stages.does: We build a design system of reusable components and rules that your designers and developers can keep using.
